The dispatch is dated the 13th of October, and you can look at the information where a certain Mr. Spicer is being quoted, and other officers of the United Nations. And in the third from the bottom, it says: "[In English] Bosnians had said they were too busy with the clashes near Orlovo, north of Sarajevo, to attend to inspections ..." [Interpretation] Thus, in our opinion, Witness, sir, this is not a conflict of the two armies. This is a massacre of medical staff that is subject to the protections of the Geneva Conventions and the massacre carried out on the territory which we had handed over to you for your control. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ182
utterances.text: Let me repeat what I have already said. This action was undertaken by the Bosnian forces. We did not accept it, and what the journalist says is his responsibility, but we made sure that this dramatic event was followed by consequences. Unfortunately, we were unable to find the perpetrators of this act.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, with all due respect, the journalist quotes Mr. Spicer and others. So this is not something that he's saying. He's quoting the journalists. Can you see that these are quotation marks, quotation marks. And this is a French agency, AFP.

utterances.speaker: KDZ182
utterances.text: Well, in this case it's not because it's a French agency that I must take for granted what this journalist Mr. Spicer says. I don't know exactly who this gentleman was.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we look at this page, what Spicer says. Spicer said: "[In English] Sarajevo Sector commander had strongly protested a Bosnian decision to pull out of a planned inspection of DMZ by senior UN Bosnian and Serb generals to ensure that the zone was being respected by both sides." [Interpretation] Spicer said that UNPROFOR officers and UNPROFOR commanders were protesting because the Muslim side was not willing to participate in the investigation. According to your knowledge, was any investigation launched?

utterances.speaker: KDZ182
utterances.text: The protest was very clear. What the journalist says is something else. There was a very firm protest on the UNPROFOR side. The investigation conducted by the UN forces enabled us to understand that this had been done by the Bosnian forces. And let me repeat: We were unable, despite a large operation launched by the UN, to find those people that had committed this act.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we tender this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I don't -- I've been looking for the document in my printouts. Is this one page? Is it the page we've been looking at?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: It's more than that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, if I can reserve my position. Just give me a moment to look at the entirety of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Well, in the meantime, can you continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You also claimed on this basis that two armies clashed there. On page 57 of your statement, you say: "[In English] The Serbs reacted a few days later by shelling and firing into the city, about which I issued a written protest on October the 10th."

utterances.speaker: KDZ182
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D2466. 1D2466.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that this is a telegram sent by Ambassador Akashi, sent to Kofi Annan from Zagreb UNPROFOR HQ, on the 19th of October? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ182
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here in paragraph 1, Mr. Akashi says that on the 6th of October, he had problems relating to the withdrawal from Mount Igman and the problems caused by Brigadier Fikret, probably Prevljak." Can we now look at the next page. Everybody can read this, and I think it will be beneficial. Now, look at paragraph 4. "[In English] In spite of UNPROFOR's immediate protests on such violations of the August 1993 agreement, the BiH did not cease their activities on Igman. In fact, these increased with the use of the demilitarised zone to launch attacks on the BSA, including the one of 6th of October which resulted in a BSA command post being wiped out with threats of retaliation from the Bosnian Serb side. We have so far been able to contain the Serb side from any precipitate action by our own intervention through Operation Igman ..." and so on. [Interpretation] How come that the boss the whole presence of the United Nations in the Balkans, of course including Bosnia-Herzegovina, did not mention any retaliation on the 19th of October? Quite the contrary. He is saying that the Serbs had refrained from any retaliation as a response to an intervention from the UN.

utterances.speaker: KDZ182
utterances.text: I believe you should ask him why he doesn't mention it in the cable. Allow me an observation though. These violations of the DMZ was one of my main concerns, and I will add that they were military actions in October, at the end of October, to make sure that the Bosnian forces leave the demilitarised zone. And it is a French UNPROFOR unit which carried out a military operation in order to oust Fikret's units which were located in Kupak [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, my question is this: Why isn't there any trace that the Serbs carried out retaliation? Quite the contrary. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: First of all, confirm my understanding we're not in private session, and if so, I will be seeking some redactions and I'll identify those for the Court in a moment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: I was going to raise that issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I just -- then I rose because I thought if we continued, we should address that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes. There are matters which I think need to be considered for redaction because they are routes to identification. But that can be done in a moment. We've got about ten minutes left for today, Dr. Karadzic, if you want to assess your remainder of your cross-examination on that basis.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It is written here that the UN protest was issued on the 10th of October. Are you trying to say that this retaliation took place before the 10th of October?

utterances.speaker: KDZ182
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your statement, you say -- in your statement, you say, page 57, towards the bottom: "[In English] The Serbs reacted a few days later by shelling and firing into the city, about which I issued a written protest on the 10th of October.

utterances.speaker: KDZ182
utterances.text: Yes. I protested on the 10th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However, in another place you say that after the meeting with Mladic on Jahorina on the 10th of October, that this retaliation took place after that meeting.

utterances.speaker: KDZ182
utterances.text: I do not know the specific date. I do remember the date of the meeting which took place on the 10th of October in Jahorina. When the retaliation took place, I'm not able to provide a specific date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D3379.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm sure you will agree that it happened before the 13th or the 19th of October. Is that correct? Mr. Witness, we saw the first text of the 13th of October. Now we see that the same news agency has printed an article on the 31st of October, and Akashi sent his report on the 19th, and in none of these documents is there any reference to the retaliation that you are mentioning. And it says here that the Bosnian government forces opened fire at the UN aeroplane operating in and out of Sarajevo airport Monday. And then it goes on to say: "[In English] Lieutenant-Colonel Bernard Labarsouque said shots were fired by the Muslim soldiers on the Butmir side of the airport at the foot of Mount Igman." [Interpretation] A little bit down. "[In English] Earlier in the day, an Ilyushin transport plane was hit by a stray bullet while on the tarmac. The reason for the firing was not known, but some hardline Muslim soldiers, based near Butmir, have objected to efforts by the UN to force them out of the -- of a demilitarised zone on Mount Igman. A tentative agreement on their withdrawal was reached Monday by UN Sector Sarajevo ..." and so on. [Interpretation] What was this Ilyushin plane carrying?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't mean to interrupt, but while the accused paused, I thought I would rise for the suggested redactions, which would be 75 -- page 75, lines 23 through 24; page 76, lines 4 through 5, and line 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: All right. Some of that is in hand, but I would agree with it. Sorry to interrupt, Mr. Witness. Can you answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, very simply, I am not in a position to tell you what was in the Ilyushin, and I believe that I was never aware of what that plane was -- was carrying. It was up to the persons in charge of logistics. It was probably goods, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Humanitarian aid, I presume, because that was the most frequent cargo.

utterances.speaker: KDZ182
utterances.text: It could have been humanitarian aid. It could have been equipment needed by UNPROFOR for its own operations, and perhaps also for soldiers more generally. I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this document admitted into evidence? I believe we have time for only one more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Yes. That's been confirmed that there was such an incident. It can be admitted. And one last question then, Dr. Karadzic. There was another document, Mr. Tieger, that you were considering the admission of, the agency report, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I haven't had it -- I see it wasn't on the list of documents we have, but I'm not going to object to that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: So be it. Then that will be admitted as well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. 1D3381 will be Exhibit D1120. And 1D3379 will be Exhibit D1121.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you. Dr. Karadzic, I think we've got to leave it there. I think it is now quarter to. Are there any other matters that we need to deal with before we rise today?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I received some -- I think, in response to the Court's earlier inquiry about completion of witnesses and so on, expressing some concern about even completing the witness who's currently -- whose testimony has been interrupted. The suggestion and some concern about the inability to complete that testimony before the -- the end of next week, before the adjournment. The one suggestion was extra sitting time, and one suggestion was indeed extra sitting time after the Seselj Chamber. I think that may come late in the day, but I'm happy -- I want to alert the Court to the fact that that's being looked into. If the Court considers that we should continue to focus on those calculations and even consider the possibility of extra sessions during the course of this week, even today, I'll be happy to liaise with the Court Officer and let them know where we are. That would mean, of course, everyone needs to stay in contact if there's any possibility of today. I'm not sure that's fair at this point, but I wanted to give full transparency to give the Court the benefit of the information I've been receiving.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. No, it wouldn't be possible today, but if you could deal with this by e-mail, I think that's probably the answer. Mr. Witness, thank you very much for your attendance today. I'm sorry that there have been some delays, and we will sit again at 9.00 tomorrow morning. Thank you.
